Greece's ruling New Democracy party remains above 30% in a new Opinion Poll survey for Action 24, but its projected 122 seats in the 300-seat parliament would leave it well short of the 151 needed to govern alone.
New Democracy stands at 30.3% in vote estimate, with Alexis Tsipras's new ELAS party second at 15.9%, a gap of 14.4 points. PASOK is third at 12.3%, followed by the Communist Party at 7.2% and Greek Solution at 6.8%.

A clear majority of Greeks want a change of government, yet the opposition is too divided to threaten Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, a new Marc poll for ANT1 television suggests, leaving his party the front-runner for next year's election without a majority to govern alone.
Some 54.1% want political change and 41.1% prefer stability. Only 36.7% approve of the government's record, while 62.7% disapprove.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis has warned that Greece will not accept cuts to EU farm and cohesion funding, that he can't promise a budget deal by December, and that Europe should not expect a rescue on energy prices, only more room for countries to spend.
